action.defines: A permission: what a role may do, the screens it shows on and the endpoints that enforce it.
action.label: Action

app.defines: A shell of the product with its own template and users.
app.label: App

assertion.defines: An atomic, sourced claim with a confidence; every row cites the claims behind it.
assertion.label: Assertion

auth-scheme.defines: How a caller proves who they are, and which endpoints use it.
auth-scheme.label: Auth scheme

bet.defines: A belief we commit resources to about closing opportunities, with a stated way to find out we're wrong; if it holds, it makes a goal true.

amplifies.note: App. B, strength weak; lateral — a checked reference, no edge

claimed_by.note: who holds the inherited claim; a project may make it a ref

collapse.note: what falls if the bet is wrong

inherited.note: a client's settled hypothesis restated as a bet (D5)

bet.label: Bet

boundary.defines: Who operates a group of nodes.
boundary.label: Boundary

capability.defines: A durable area of the product, with its own journey, data and rules, that realises one or more bets.

boundary_owner.note: who owns the capability's edge with other capabilities or outside systems

journeys.note: journey-map ids where the vault has that kind

linear.note: the tracker epic it maps to, when the team tracks Backlog Items there

proposal.note: the proposal line items it was priced under

capability.label: Capability
capability.test: Can you draw its journey and data shape, and will it outlive the current work?

collection.defines: A stored collection: fields, references, indexes and the service that owns it.
collection.label: Collection

component.defines: A reusable UI part at an atomic-design level, with its parts and the variants use cases need.
component.label: Component

concern.defines: A cross-cutting runtime risk and the sequences it touches.
concern.label: Concern

conformance.defines: A dated reading of one model row against one rule that governs it: who checked it, where, and when.

against.note: <kind>:<id> of the rule it was read against

at.note: where it was read: a commit, page or build

row.note: <kind>:<id> of the row that was read

conformance.label: Conformance check

connection.defines: A link between two nodes with its own protocol, status and evidence.
connection.label: Connection

constraint.defines: Restriction that must be honoured: a regulator's rule, a contract, a mandated stack, a budget.

governs.note: the model rows this house rule governs, as <kind>:<id> (field:<collection>.<path> for a field); never a flow or screen

value_defs.domain: A domain truth the client states in its own words (a house rule).
value_defs.policy: An outside or company policy the product must honour (an obligation).
value_defs.product: A choice about this product that could have gone the other way (a product rule).

constraint.label: Constraint

core-system.defines: A design-system building block that groups components and uses tokens.
core-system.label: Core system

decision.defines: Choice made or pending, with the options considered and rejected.

confirmed_by.note: who attested it (Confirmed by); decider is who made the call and never attests

products.note: the products an account decision applies to (the log's **Products:** line; * = every product); the model union keeps it to them

refs.note: the non-claim wikilinks the log entry carries (sources, artifacts)

significance.note: hard-to-change | cross-capability | constrains-later | persisted-data | external-commitment | regulatory (the draft's §4 checklist)

supersedes_text.note: a configured log's supersede reference that names no entry; kept as written

decision.label: Decision

driver.defines: The business value the client wants from the work: one of Atomic's twelve Business Value options, or a product-market-fit lever. It is why the sponsor signs off.
driver.label: Driver
driver.test: Would the sponsor name this as a reason to fund the work?

effort.defines: An iteration-sized package of implementation work owned by one developer: builds a slice of one or more specs, or all of them, and is the running log of the plan, decisions, deviations and follow-ups.
effort.label: Effort

endpoint.defines: An API route: the roles that may call it, the service behind it, the data it reads and writes, the events it emits.

reads_fields.note: <collection>.<path> the endpoint reads; generated into _generated/endpoint-fields.yaml by kb-site reconcile endpoint-fields, never hand-edited

endpoint.label: Endpoint

enum.defines: A named set of values used across the model, either literal or sourced from another kind's keys.
enum.label: Enum

environment.defines: Where the deployables run: local, staging, production.
environment.label: Environment

event.defines: A typed timeline row written by an endpoint that may move a status.
event.label: Event

falsifier.defines: Pre-agreed evidence that would kill the bet.
falsifier.label: Falsifier

feature.defines: Something a user can recognise that can ship on its own, delivering part of a capability; groups the use cases that deliver it.
feature.label: Feature
feature.test: Can a user recognise it and can it ship alone?

flag.defines: A marker carried alongside the status.
flag.label: Flag

flow.defines: One primary actor reaching one goal from a trigger to an end state.

activation.note: this onboarding flow ends at the user's first value

adoption.note: absent = usage; onboarding flows are ordered by next

governed_by.note: a hand override for a use case no rule, status or field path reaches, as <kind>:<id>

moves.note: the transitions the use case makes, each "<from>><to>"; both ends among its statuses (validators/flow_moves.py)

origin.note: migration-placeholder: written only so a migrated screen has a flow walking it; `kb-site migrate check` warns while one remains (placeholder-flows)

stage.note: none: the use case moves through no status on purpose (statuses: []; spec 2026-10-23 §6.2), which silences status-unstaged-flow

flow.label: Use case

goal.defines: What the client wants to be true when the engagement is done: what a bet makes true if it holds.
goal.label: Goal
goal.test: Could we tell at the end whether it's true?

indicator.defines: A measure on exactly one driver, goal or bet.

benchmark.note: <pmf-level>/<benchmark> (method pmf-levels.yaml): the PMF benchmark its threshold is taken from; empty outside B2B SaaS

indicator.label: Indicator

journey.defines: A backbone goal on the story map.
journey.label: Activity

journey-map.defines: One persona's current-state journey: its scenario, phases and opportunities; the phases name use cases.
journey-map.label: Journey map

jurisdiction.defines: A jurisdiction whose law an engine rule applies or names (_engines.yaml `jurisdictions`), linked to those rules.
jurisdiction.label: Jurisdiction

masked-field.defines: A field hidden from certain roles while the rest of the record shows.
masked-field.label: Masked field

node.defines: A deployable, store, external system or actor on the architecture picture.
node.label: Node

non-screen.defines: A rendered surface with no screen id that a flow touches: an email, an SMS, a printed slip.
non-screen.label: Surface

notification.defines: One kind of message the product sends: who receives it, on which channels, how urgently, whether it is on by default and whether the recipient may switch it off.

events.note: the event types that fire it; a checked name, no edge

open.note: an open-question claim the row waits on

recipients.note: {<user code | outside recipient>: {channels, default, mandatory, opens, sees}}; channels name notification-channel rows

template.note: the email template that carries its wording; a checked name, no edge

notification.label: Notification

notification-channel.defines: A way a notification reaches its recipient (in the product, email, text message, webhook), and when it exists.

open.note: an open-question claim the channel waits on

notification-channel.label: Notification channel

notification-class.defines: How urgent a notification is, and so how it is delivered and whether a recipient may switch it off.
notification-class.label: Notification class

notification-group.defines: A heading notifications are grouped under on the notification map.
notification-group.label: Notification group

opportunity.defines: A specific gap, found in research, between today and a driver's business value; phrased as a gap, never a solution.
opportunity.label: Opportunity
opportunity.test: Can you point to the evidence?

org.defines: The organisation a user belongs to.
org.label: Org

outcome.defines: Measurable result by which a goal's achievement is known.
outcome.label: Outcome

pattern.defines: A recurring interface decision: the problem it prevents, the rule, its parts and variants, and the tokens and principles it rests on.

value_defs.agreed: Decided; its checks fail the build.
value_defs.deprecated: Being retired; screens still drawing it are listed.

pattern.label: Pattern

persona.defines: A composite of the people behind one or more roles: goals, pains and jobs to be done.
persona.label: Persona

pmf-assessment.defines: Where one of the client's products is on the product-market fit ladder in one market, on a date: the level, its weakest dimension and its weakest P.

market.note: set when the product is assessed in more than one market

pmf-assessment.label: PMF assessment

principle.defines: A design principle that settles trade-offs.
principle.label: Principle

quality.defines: A measurable bar the product must meet over time: how fast, how reliable, how usable, how it is updated and how long it is supported.
quality.label: Quality target

question.defines: An open question, who can answer it, the work it holds up and the other questions its answer unblocks.

answerableBy.note: stakeholder ids: who holds the answer

askIn.note: a session the question is booked into

blocksHat.note: hats (.kb/config/hats.md): the work it holds up

gates.note: a phase exit criterion it holds open, worded as phase-state.md does

question.label: Open question

release.defines: A horizontal slice of the story map that ships together.
release.label: Release

requirement.defines: A testable shall statement with acceptance criteria; functional per module, non-functional per category.

horizon.note: an override of the roll-up from the flows it governs (V9)

tags.note: spike: in the first release but blocked on a de-risking question (a tag, not a horizon)

requirement.label: Requirement

resource.defines: A group of API endpoints under one path family.
resource.label: Resource

role.defines: A permission role: what a user code may do, and what it inherits from.
role.label: Role

rule.defines: One block of an engine's program: a step, a test or a wait, with the statuses, records, roles, events, terms and jurisdictions it names, reads, writes, moves or records.

block.note: the block's id in its engine; the row's id is <engine>.<block>

collections.note: the records it names; a setting it reads is not a link to the setting's record

events.note: the events it names and the one that starts it

flows.note: the flows this engine step drives (the step's flows: key)

jurisdictions.note: those it names, and those whose law it applies (the jurisdictions spec's kinds: example, applied_by)

moves.note: both ends of the status move it makes

name.note: what the graph and the site title it by: the block's text

service.note: the services.yaml id of the module that owns the engine (_engines.yaml)

users.note: the roles it names, who starts it and who it notifies

rule.label: Rule

scenario.defines: A situation the product must handle, run through one or more use cases; its horizon is the latest of theirs.

decided_in.note: the source id of the demo that agreed or disputed it

effects.note: Also changes: what else QA must check

findings.note: ids in the file's findings list, or finding record ids (fnd-…) in _improvements/

label.note: the walk's short name; the title when absent

path.note: {as, steps: [{s, as, say, by, at, act, sees, shows, handoffs, events, near, later}]}: statuses, each consecutive pair a transition; events picks which of that transition's events happened; by/at/sees/handoffs/events and the near/later overrides draw the role grid (scenarios.py); act names the action of the step's screen that makes the move; shows is {<screen>: {<component>: <variant>}}, the state the step puts a seen screen's components in (validators/scenario_rows.py)

value_defs.edge: A boundary: a limit, a timing, a rare combination.
value_defs.happy: The use case goes as intended.
value_defs.unhappy: Something goes wrong and the product recovers or refuses.

rests_on.note: assertion slugs; confidence is the weakest of them

value_defs.agreed: The client agreed the expected outcome.
value_defs.proposed: Nobody on the client side has agreed the expected outcome.

steps.note: expected steps for a Given/When/Then row; a walk's steps come from its path

then.note: {state, sees, effects, never}: lists of lines

value_defs.key: A situation the product exists for.

use_cases.note: at least one; the scenario's horizon is the latest of theirs

variant_of.note: the main scenario this one is a small departure from; absent on a main scenario. One level only: the target is not itself a variant (validators/scenario_rows.py)

walk.note: the slug a walk plays under (state machine, walk-through); needs a path

scenario.label: Scenario

scope-question.defines: A fixed-choice call that draws the scope line: its options, the model rows its answer moves and the open questions it settles.

governs.note: the model rows this call moves, as <kind>:<id> (field:<collection>.<path> for a field); never a flow or screen

applies_at.note: one of alignment.knob_scopes (platform, per-tenant, per-plan, per-device…)

kind.note: policy: legal or commercial; spec-constant: hardware or firmware

override_by.note: a lower scope that may override it

shape_owner.note: stakeholder or person: who decides the question and its options

value_from.note: where the value lives; locator one of alignment.setting_sources; never the value itself

value_owner.note: who sets the value: a stakeholder, or a tenant role ("each tenant's admin")

value_agreement.note: the client's yes to the current value or default; agreement is the yes to the shape (question and options)

value_attested_in.note: one claim, decision or source: who said yes to the value (as attested_in is for the shape)

scope-question.label: Scope call

screen.defines: A page with a route, regions of components, actions leading to other screens, and access per role.

moves.note: the transitions the action makes, each "<from>><to>" as a flow's moves; each from a status the screen draws (validators/define.py)

screen.label: Screen
